note: Rewritten from the species description in Scheffrahn & Vasconcellos 2023, originally in English; the original has complete Imago and Soldier descriptions with measurements, both rewritten here; the text omits the species-by-species comparison, type material, etymology, distribution and ecology, the key to South American soldiers, and molecular and plate information; measurements follow the original (means for n=3 alates and n=2 soldiers).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate differs from most congeners in lacking an arolium between the tarsal claws and in the media giving off several branches that intersect the radial sector; the absence of an arolium is shared only with C. brevis, C. chacoensis, C. kirbyi and C. darwini, while a forewing venation in which the multi-branched media intersects the radial sector was previously known only in C. brevis, C. darwini and C. kirbyi. Among South American congeners the soldier is unique in having a head capsule that is cubic (box-like) in dorsal view and a strongly rugose, rounded and markedly protruding postclypeus; the postclypeus of C. brevis and C. chacoensis comes closest to that of the new species, but in both the head capsule constricts behind the frontal ridges. As in C. aequacornis, C. cylindroceps and C. rhicnocephalus, the frontal and genal horns project forward by equal lengths; in the new species the anterior margin of the postclypeus is rounded and the mandibles project laterally by more than half the head width, whereas in C. aequacornis the postclypeus is truncate anteriorly and the mandibles project laterally by less than half the head width.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
Head capsule and pronotum pale yellowish brown. Compound eyes obtusely triangular; ocelli pale yellow, about half the diameter of a compound eye, roundly oval, touching the eye margin. Vertex with a few short setae. Pronotum wider than the head capsule, anterior margin shallowly concave, each lateral margin with about a dozen setae. Antenna 15-segmented, relative lengths of the basal segments 2=3>4=5. Forewing subcosta merging with the costa about one-eighth of the wing length from the wing suture; wing membrane pale, veins slightly darker; costa, subcosta, radius and radial sector sclerotized, the unsclerotized media giving off several branches that intersect the radial sector, the media ending on the radial sector at about three-quarters of the wing length and thereafter forming a separate branch near the wing apex. Arolium absent.
Measurements (mm, mean; n=3): maximum head width (including compound eyes) 0.96, maximum head width (excluding compound eyes) 0.88, maximum pronotum width 0.94, maximum compound eye diameter 0.23, maximum ocellus diameter 0.12, body length 5.3, right forewing length (from wing scale) 6.90, body length with wings 8.74.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head capsule strongly rugose in dorsal view, grading from dark chestnut brown at the postclypeus to orange brown on the occiput. Widest at the posterior third, narrowest at the frontal ridges. Frontal ridges V-shaped, deeply incised medially. Posterior margin of the head capsule truncate, posterior lateral corners right-angled, lateral margins nearly parallel, together forming a cube. In profile the frontal ridges raised, the vertex unevenly concave; frontal horns bluntly tuberculate. Genal horns rounded, slightly behind the frontal horns. Pronotum steeply declivous from the vertex, narrower than the head capsule; anterior margin dark and wavy-rugose, incised medially into a rounded anterior lobe. Eye spots large, narrowly oval. Frons concave in oblique view. Postclypeus evenly convex, strongly rugose, projecting distinctly beyond the frontal ridges. Antenna 8 or 9 segments (third segment fused or free), or 10 or 11 segments (third segment fused or free). Mandibles broad and short for the genus, rugose, with a rounded basal swelling mid-ventrally, the outer edge of the blade at an angle of about 50°.
Measurements (mm, mean; n=2): head length to mandible apex 1.57, head length to genal horn apex 1.20, frontal ridge width 1.11, outer span of frontal horns 0.90, outer span of genal horns 0.95, maximum head width 1.20, minimum head width (behind frontal ridges) 1.10, head height (excluding postmentum) 0.88, maximum pronotum length 0.95, maximum pronotum width 1.12, left mandible length (apex to ventral process) 0.53.
